summary: Pulaski County, MO 100-foot steel tower in Mark Twain National Forest, allegedly built 1937; register says closed after vandalism; sources are thin.

facts.design: 100-foot steel tower, possibly an Aermotor MC-39
facts.status_note: Closed after vandalism per the on-site sign the register describes; the register says the tower is in good shape and under active surveillance

access.note: Register says the site is closed after vandalism, per a sign at the site; the closure date is not given

visit.trail_note: Reached by a short gravel road into a small grassy clearing; the site is fenced with barbed wire and closed. Do not climb.

events.note: Register says the tower was allegedly erected in 1937 as a steel tower (possibly an Aermotor MC-39 from 1934); Forest Lookouts gives 1937 as a 100-foot steel tower
Registered August 13, 2026; nominated by Audrey LaBeaume

resolved_conflicts.explanation: The register says allegedly 1937, possibly an Aermotor MC-39 from 1934; Forest Lookouts gives 1937. The story uses 1937 and flags it as uncertain, with the 1934 model year noted as possible.

notes_for_editor: Only two sources, and the register itself says resources are extremely limited. Build year is 'allegedly' 1937. Closure date unknown. No Forest Service page found; the News-Leader 2018 article returned 403 and was not read. Staffing omitted (no record found). Visit note treats the tower as closed.
